philosophy.body: Virtuous Vogue is a styling house built on one conviction: identity informs style. Style does not determine identity.

woman.title: Before any garment, there is a woman with a life.
woman.p1: Every consultation begins there: the rooms she walks into, the work she does, the family she returns to, the way she wants to be met. Her worth is not decided by her outfit, her shape, her budget, a label or her ability to follow a trend.
woman.p2: Once that is clear, the clothes become easy. They become a language she already speaks, rather than a test she keeps failing.

why.title: Because too much fashion advice makes women feel smaller.
why.p1: The industry sells inadequacy and calls it aspiration. Fix your flaws, hide your problem areas, buy the thing that will finally make you enough. Virtuous Vogue was founded to do the opposite: to help women see what is already working and build from it.
why.p2: Fashion is the language. Identity is the message. Style is how you communicate it. Our role is to help you speak it fluently, in your own accent.
why.quote1: You give what you wear relevance.
why.quote2: What you wear does not give you relevance.

selling.title: We shop your closet first.
selling.p1: Closet Remix, our wardrobe technology, is built to compose outfits from what you already own. It only names a purchase when a true gap exists, and it labels it optional. Our curated Edit will arrive later, and it will follow the same rule.
selling.p2: Styling is the business. Selling, when it comes, is in service of it.

founder.title: A stylist who would rather listen first.
founder.p1: Virtuous Vogue was founded in Douala by a stylist who spent years watching capable, accomplished women apologise for their wardrobes. The studio exists so they can stop.
founder.p2: Her approach is quiet, specific and practical: understand the woman, read the wardrobe honestly, and make the next morning easier than the last one.
founder.quote1: I'm not here to tell you to dress like me.
founder.quote2: I'm here to help you discover how to dress like you.

sections.title: What we collect
body: Account details (name, email, phone), the answers you give in the Style Studio, wardrobe photographs you upload, consultation notes and booking and payment records.
We collect only what a styling relationship needs, and we tell you why each time we ask.

sections.title: Photographs
body: Wardrobe and Colour Lens photographs are processed to suggest outfits or preview colour. They are stored privately under your account, encrypted in transit and at rest, and never used to train models.
You can delete any image, or your whole account, at any time from Privacy settings. Colour Lens images are discarded immediately unless you choose to save them.

sections.title: Payments
body: Payments are processed by licensed gateways (Mobile Money and card providers). We store the transaction reference and status, never your card number or Mobile Money PIN.

sections.title: Your rights
body: You can download your data, correct it, or delete it from your Style Passport. Write to us for anything the dashboard does not cover.

sections.title: Analytics
body: We use privacy-conscious analytics without cookies that track you across sites. Conversion events are counted, not people.

sections.title: Consultations
body: A booking is confirmed when the deposit is received or when the stylist confirms a request. Pricing is shared before any payment is taken.
You may reschedule or cancel up to 24 hours before a session. Deposits for later cancellations may be retained.

sections.title: Style Studio
body: Style Compass, Colour Lens and Closet Remix are assistive tools. Their outputs are directions and previews, not professional verdicts, and the stylist's interpretation always takes precedence.

sections.title: Content
body: Magazine stories and campaign imagery are the property of Virtuous Vogue. Campaign imagery is art-directed and generated for the brand; the women depicted are not clients.

sections.title: Liability
body: We do our best work every time. We are not liable for purchases you make on your own initiative or for third-party services such as payment gateways and calendars.
